Can you please triage immediately and advise on a mitigation (fallback to older model, increased rate allowance, anything)? We need ETA on remediation and whether this qualifies for SLA credit.

Subject: Re: High latency and 429s on /v1/generate — urgent

Status update from infra: short version: confirmed misaligned refill + routing fallback loop. Long version below.

Findings:
- The token refill task for tenant_acme (refill job id: refill-acme-2029-03-18) was being delayed by up to 2.6s due to a scheduling regression introduced in commit 9f3a2 that changed the refill cadence when a node's load crosses the "safety_threshold". The check incorrectly ignored tenant-based exemptions.
- When refill is delayed, requests exhaust the burst bucket and are routed to fallback nodes (route policy: latency_prefalled->fallback) which have smaller per-tenant capacities; those nodes then queue and return 429s.
- Continuous batching heuristics also increased head-of-line blocking for medium-length prompts (~512 tokens).

Actions taken (08:35–08:40):
- Applied emergency override to tenant_acme: token_bucket_capacity set to 2x (was 1200 tokens -> 2400 tokens) and burst_window_ms extended from 2000ms -> 5000ms for a 5% canary.
- Disabled the safety_threshold exemption check that was preventing tenant refills when nodes were hot (hotfix 9f3a2-revert).
- Temporarily relaxed continuous-batching for model:v3-cust to avoid long queueing (per-canary).

Observations (08:40–08:55):
- 429s for the canary slice dropped from 8% -> 1.1%.
- P95 latency for canary improved to ~480ms; overall customer p95 is trending down but still elevated (~1.1s) while rollout continues.

Next steps:
- Connor to roll the override to 25% traffic if metrics hold for 20m.
- We need product to review routing capacity allocation for fallback nodes (Lauren).
- Suggest an immediate config patch to ensure refill jobs respect tenant exemptions going forward and add an alert when refill delay > 1s.

I will keep monitoring and post graphs to CIS-1729.

— Marcus
SRE Manager
Redwood Inference

Marissa — bringing to exec level because the customer is requesting SLA credit and full mitigation. Quick summary and ask:

Summary:
- Root cause: tenant-specific token refill was delayed by a scheduling regression (commit 9f3a2) that ignored tenant exemptions when node "safety_threshold" was crossed. This created a refill gap and a routing fallback loop that produced 429s and higher latency during bursts.
- Remediation: hotfix rolled (9f3a2-revert), emergency overrides applied (token_bucket_capacity x2, burst_window_ms +3s) and continuous-batching relaxed for affected model. Canary shows 429 -> ~1% and p95 reduction to ~480–520ms for canary slice. Broad rollout in progress.
- Customer impact: partial; majority of traffic still warming up to improvements. Customer has asked about SLA credit.

Requested decisions / asks:
1) Approve one-time service credit up to 5% of monthly spend for Acme if final impact window > 30m. (Monica can provide exact numbers and scope).
2) Approve expedited change to routing allocation for fallback nodes (product + infra) to prevent capacity cliffs — target ETA 5 business days.
3) Approve a postmortem and customer-facing RCA within 72 hours with concrete remediation items (alerting on refill delays, stricter routing guardrails, and regression test).

I'll coordinate the customer call and the RCA draft. If approved, Monica — please prepare the proposed credit and communications plan.

— Stephanie
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
